case_title: Shyamal Ghosh v. State of West Bengal
aggravating_circumstances: Absconding immediately after the incident, disposal of the body, use of weapon, presence of multiple accused
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of all charges and sentenced to death
high_court_outcome: Affirmed conviction except for s.379/34 IPC, sentenced to life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 5000/-
neutral_facts: The prosecution case is that the deceased had constructed some shop on his land. The accused persons demanded Rs. 40,000 from the deceased towards 'Tola Mastani Salami' for the construction of the shops. The deceased refused to succumb to the demand and therefore, the accused threatened to murder him. On the day of the incident, at 9.00 P.M., the deceased had gone to one place in respect of his business, on a bicycle. From there, he returned to his house at 10.00 P.M. On the way, he was restrained by the accused. The accused killed him by strangulation. Thereafter, they cut the body into pieces with a sharp cutting weapon and after putting the same in gunny bags, carried them in a van in the night of the following day and left the same at some place. A witness saw those gunny bags and reported the matter to the police. FIR was lodged and case was registered under s. 302/201/341 IPC against unknown miscreants. The van was recovered on the basis of the driver's statement. All the accused were arrested on different dates. The cycle used by the deceased was recovered. The accused were charged under s. 302, 201, 379, 411 rlw. s. 34 IPC. The prosecution has proved the complete chain of events, including the last seen together theory, the strangulation of the deceased by the accused, and the disposal of the body in gunny bags into a van. The accused absconded immediately after the incident, which supports the prosecution case.
